arxiv-2101-05383.title: Self-driven criticality in a stochastic epidemic model
arxiv-2101-05383.creator: Gil Ariel, Yoram Louzoun
arxiv-2101-05383.description: Abstract We present a generic epidemic model with stochastic parameters, in which the dynamics self-organize to a critical state with suppressed exponential growth. More precisely, the dynamics evolve into a quasi-steady-state, where the effective reproduction rate fluctuates close to the critical value one for a long period, as indeed observed for different epidemics.

arxiv-2105-14244.title: Learning Graphon Autoencoders for Generative Graph Modeling
arxiv-2105-14244.creator: Hongteng Xu, Peilin Zhao, Junzhou Huang, Dixin Luo
arxiv-2105-14244.description: Abstract Graphon is a nonparametric model that generates graphs with arbitrary sizes and can be induced from graphs easily. Based on this model, we propose a novel algorithmic framework called graphon autoencoder to build an interpretable and scalable graph generative model.

arxiv-2201-11451.title: Setting AI in context: A case study on defining the context and operational design domain for automated driving Thanks: This project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation program under grant agreement No 957197.
arxiv-2201-11451.creator: Hans-Martin Heyn, Padmini Subbiah, Jennifer Linder, Eric Knauss, Olof Eriksson
arxiv-2201-11451.description: Abstract [Context and motivation] For automated driving systems, the operational context needs to be known in order to state guarantees on performance and safety. The operational design domain (ODD) is an abstraction of the operational context, and its definition is an integral part of the system development process.

arxiv-2311-07227.title: CARTOS: A Charging-Aware Real-Time Operating System for Intermittent Batteryless Devices
arxiv-2311-07227.creator: Mohsen Karimi, Yidi Wang, Youngbin Kim, Yoojin Lim, Hyoseung Kim
arxiv-2311-07227.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mohsen Karimi, Yidi Wang, Youngbin Kim, Yoojin Lim, Hyoseung Kim. This paper presents CARTOS, a charging-aware real-time operating system designed to enhance the functionality of intermittently-powered batteryless devices (IPDs) for various Internet of Things (IoT) applications. While IPDs offer significant advantages such as extended lifespan and operability in extreme environments, they pose unique challenges, including the need to ensure forward progress of program execution amidst variable energy availability and maintaining reliable real-time time behavior during power disruptions.

arxiv-2312-05433.title: Stochastic Directly-Follows Process Discovery Using Grammatical Inference
arxiv-2312-05433.creator: Hanan Alkhammash (🖂) and Artem Polyvyanyy and Alistair Moffat
arxiv-2312-05433.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hanan Alkhammash (🖂) and Artem Polyvyanyy and Alistair Moffat. Starting with a collection of traces generated by process executions, process discovery is the task of constructing a simple model that describes the process, where simplicity is often measured in terms of model size. The challenge of process discovery is that the process of interest is unknown, and that while the input traces constitute positive examples of process executions, no negative examples are available.

arxiv-2402-06788.title: Magnetic field-temperature phase diagram of spin-1/2 triangular lattice antiferromagnet KYbSe 2
arxiv-2402-06788.creator: Sangyun Lee, Andrew J. Woods, Minseong Lee, Shengzhi Zhang, Eun Sang Choi, A. O. Scheie, D. A. Tennant, J. Xing, A. S. Sefat, R. Movshovich
arxiv-2402-06788.description: Abstract A quantum spin liquid (QSL) is a state of matter characterized by fractionalized quasiparticle excitations, quantum entanglement, and a lack of long-range magnetic order. However, QSLs have evaded definitive experimental observation. Several Yb 3+ -based triangular lattice antiferromagnets with effective S S = 1 2 \frac{1}{2} have been suggested to stabilize the QSL state as the ground state.

arxiv-2501-05390.title: Self-propulsion and self-rotation of an inertial chiral active Ornstein-Uhlenbeck particle
arxiv-2501-05390.creator: F Sahala, M Muhsin, M Sahoo
arxiv-2501-05390.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by F Sahala, M Muhsin, M Sahoo. We investigate the transport feature of an inertial chiral active Ornstein-Uhlenbeck particle moving on a two-dimensional surface. Using both analytical approach and numerical simulations, we have exactly explored the transient and steady-state behavior of the particle by analyzing the simulated particle trajectories, probability distribution functions for position and velocity, mean square displacement, mean square velocity, and effective kinetic temperature of the medium.

arxiv-2501-08465.title: Predicting Performance of Object Detection Models in Electron Microscopy Using Random Forests Thanks: Citation : Authors. Title. Pages…. DOI:000000/11111.
arxiv-2501-08465.creator: Ni Li, Ryan Jacobs, Vidit Agrawal, Dane Morgan, Matthew Lynch, Kevin Field
arxiv-2501-08465.description: Abstract Quantifying prediction uncertainty when applying object detection models to new, unlabeled datasets is critical in applied machine learning. This study introduces an approach to estimate the performance of deep learning-based object detection models for quantifying defects in transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images, focusing on detecting irradiation-induced cavities in TEM images of metal alloys.

arxiv-2505-16044.title: Multimodal Biomarkers for Schizophrenia: Towards Individual Symptom Severity Estimation
arxiv-2505-16044.creator: Gowtham, Philip, Sonia, Deanna, Carol
arxiv-2505-16044.description: Abstract Studies on schizophrenia assessments using deep learning typically treat it as a classification task to detect the presence or absence of the disorder, oversimplifying the condition and reducing its clinical applicability. This traditional approach overlooks the complexity of schizophrenia, limiting its practical value in healthcare settings.

arxiv-2508-07854.title: Challenges in Mixed Reality in Assisting Adults with ADHD Symptoms DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Envisioning the Future of Accessible Immersive Technology; September 1st, 2024; Karlsruhe, Germany Mensch und Computer 2024 Workshop: Envisioning the Future of Accessible Immersive Technology, Septemb
arxiv-2508-07854.creator: Valerie Tan, Jens Gerken
arxiv-2508-07854.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Valerie Tan, Jens Gerken. In this position paper, we discuss symptoms of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in adults, as well as available forms of treatment or assistance in the context of mixed reality. Mixed reality offers many potentials for assisting adults with symptoms commonly found in (but not limited to) ADHD, but the availability of mixed reality solutions is not only limited commercially, but also limited in terms of proof-of-concept prototypes.

arxiv-2508-21577.title: Transport Model Investigation of NCQ Scaling and the Hadronic–Partonic Transition in Au+Au Collisions
arxiv-2508-21577.creator: Li-Ke Liu, Shusu Shi
arxiv-2508-21577.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Li-Ke Liu, Shusu Shi. We investigate elliptic flow ( v 2 v_{2} ) in Au+Au collisions at s NN = 3.0 \sqrt{s_{\text{NN}}}=3.0 and 4.5 GeV using hadronic and partonic transport models, including JAM, SMASH, AMPT-Hadronic Cascade, and AMPT-String Melting.

pmc-10810990.title: ΔFosB is part of a homeostatic mechanism that protects the epileptic brain from further deterioration
pmc-10810990.creator: Jerome Clasadonte, Tania Deprez, Gabriel S. Stephens, Georges Mairet-Coello, Pierre-Yves Cortin, Maxime Boutier, Aurore Frey, Jeannie Chin, Marek Rajman
pmc-10810990.description: Activity induced transcription factor ΔFosB plays a key role in different CNS disorders including epilepsy, Alzheimer’s disease, and addiction. Recent findings suggest that ΔFosB drives cognitive deficits in epilepsy and together with the emergence of small molecule inhibitors of ΔFosB activity makes it an interesting therapeutic target.

pmc-11482570.title: An Automated Clubbed Fingers Detection System Based on YOLOv8 and U-Net: A Tool for Early Prediction of Lung and Cardiovascular Diseases
pmc-11482570.creator: Wen-Shin Hsu, Guan-Tsen Liu, Su-Juan Chen, Si-Yu Wei, Wei-Hsun Wang
pmc-11482570.description: Background/Objectives: Lung and cardiovascular diseases are leading causes of mortality worldwide, yet early detection remains challenging due to the subtle symptoms. Digital clubbing, characterized by the bulbous enlargement of the fingertips, serves as an early indicator of these diseases. This study aims to develop an automated system for detecting digital clubbing using deep-learning models for real-time monitoring and early intervention.

pmc-11600174.title: Effect of Thermal Stress on Morphology in High-Performance Organic Photovoltaic Blends
pmc-11600174.creator: Haoyu Zhao, Nathaniel Prine, Soumya Kundu, Guorong Ma, Xiaodan Gu
pmc-11600174.description: Thermal stress is a critical factor causing long-term instability in bulk heterojunction (BHJ) layers of organic photovoltaic (OPV) devices. This study provides direct insights into the thermal properties of Y6, PM6, and their binary blends by employing fast differential scanning calorimetry (flash DSC) to analyze their chain dynamics.

pmc-11712804.title: Phase 3 Trial of Oral Anti‐Amyloid Agent ALZ‐801/Valiltramiprosate in APOE4/4 Homozygotes with Early Alzheimer’s Disease: Baseline Characteristics and Prevalence of Comorbid Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy
pmc-11712804.creator: Aidan Power, David Watson, Susan Abushakra, Emer MacSweeney, Anton P. Porsteinsson, Marwan N. Sabbagh, Earvin Liang, Rosalind McLaine, Mercè Boada, Jón Snædal, Susan Flint, Winnie Pak, John A. Hey, Martin Tolar
pmc-11712804.description: BackgroundALZ‐801/valiltramiprosate, an oral small molecule inhibitor of amyloid oligomer formation, is being evaluated in a Phase 3 trial in APOE4/4 Early AD subjects (APOLLOE4). Topline results are expected in 3Q 2024. APOE4 is a major risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) with a gene‐dose effect.

pmc-12502512.title: Obesity competencies for healthcare professionals: a scoping review
pmc-12502512.creator: Kenneth Verboven, Camilla Wikström-Grotell, Susanna Lehtinen-Jacks, Mary E. Davis, Gráinne O’Donoghue, Pipsa P. A. Tuominen, Anouk Agten, Fiona Curran, Caitriona Cunningham
pmc-12502512.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe Obesity Policy Engagement Network (OPEN)-EU manifesto, led by the European Association for the Study of Obesity (EASO), underscores the urgent need for enhanced, evidence-based education for healthcare professionals (HCPs) involved in obesity care.

pmc-12650028.title: Fetal Sex Modulates Hofbauer Cells’ Response to Diabetes in Human Placenta
pmc-12650028.creator: Zdenek Tauber, Max Mrstik, Adela Burianova, Katerina Koubova, Katerina Cizkova
pmc-12650028.description: Background: Hofbauer cells (HBCs) are fetal-origin macrophages in the placental villous stroma that contribute to immune tolerance at the feto–maternal interface. They predominantly display an M2 phenotype, characterized by CD206 expression. Methods: Using immunohistochemistry and morphometric analysis, we quantified HBCs, assessed CD206 intensity and morphology, and evaluated apoptotic body accumulation in placental villi.

pmc-13263197.title: Long-term safety and pulmonary function stabilization with nintedanib in systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease, 2020–2025: a real-world retrospective study from a reference centre
pmc-13263197.creator: Stylianos Panopoulos, Vasiliki Poulia, Nikolaos Vlachogiannis, Vasiliki-Kalliopi Bournia, Maria G Tektonidou, Petros P Sfikakis
pmc-13263197.description: Randomized trials have demonstrated that nintedanib is beneficial for Systemic Sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD) with an acceptable safety profile. We evaluated the long-term safety and efficacy of nintedanib in a real-world SSc-ILD cohort. Medical records of SSc patients receiving nintedanib for newly diagnosed fibrotic or progressive ILD between 2020 and 2025 in our center were retrospectively reviewed.

pmc-13473110.title: Species-specific assessment of climate change vulnerability in Himalayan Pikas and identification of at-risk elevational and latitudinal zones
pmc-13473110.creator: Nishma Dahal, Pritam Chhetri, Sunil Kumar, Rajat Nayak, Vineet K Dubey, Aashna Sharma, Barry R Noon, Uma Ramakrishnan
pmc-13473110.description: Climate change is rapidly transforming high-altitude ecosystems, placing cold-adapted species at risk. We assessed the vulnerability of four Himalayan Pika species (Ochotona macrotis, O. roylei, O. nubrica, and O. sikimaria) by integrating species distribution models with landscape metrics and sensitivity indices. Using verified occurrence records and bioclimatic variables, we projected habitat suitability under moderate (SSP 2-4.5) and extreme (SSP 5-8.
